evals.expected_output: Routes to context/e2e.md. FIRST runs prerequisite check: verifies the project's orchestrator tooling is available, Playwright CLI available (@playwright/cli installed — primary browser automation path; MCP is disabled by default), app running. If prerequisites are missing, hard-fails: STOPs (does not attempt workarounds) AND writes a structured verification-environment gap report to the run's evidence output naming what is missing (keys, CLIs, MCPs, or environments) and what the operator must provide, with remediation steps (e.g., 'npm install -g @playwright/cli'). If available, resolves the config surface (recording, browser_mode) across its layers, then proceeds with health check, endpoint verification, and evidence capture. References the playwright plugin's skill for browser mechanics when enabled.

evals.prompt: How do I live-test a change to an MCP server with no UI?
evals.expected_output: Routes to context/non-ui.md. Maps the MCP-server surface to its smoke-test invocation: unit-level coverage plus the JSON-RPC initialize stdio-handshake pattern. Does not demand browser evidence for a non-UI surface.

evals.name: prerequisites-pass-config-resolved-drive-delegated
evals.expected_output: Prerequisites pass, so the run does not stop. Step 2 resolves recording and browser_mode per key across the user-global, team, and local layers of .claude/testing/e2e.md and reports which layer supplied each effective value. Step 3 delegates the drive loop to a subagent, passes the resolved browser_mode and recording through, and consumes only the evidence paths it returns.
expectations: Reads every layer of the config surface and merges recording and browser_mode per key
Reports which layer supplied each effective value
Delegates the drive loop to a subagent instead of driving the browser in its own context
Passes the resolved browser_mode and recording through to the executor
Returns only evidence paths, not browser session output

evals.name: native-step-skip-when-bundled-run-disabled
evals.prompt: /testing:run-e2e the login flow. disableBundledSkills is set in settings and the project has no orchestrator configuration.
evals.expected_output: The bundled run skill is disabled for model invocation, so the Native step is skipped and the result block records the refusal. The evidence output opens with the result block, names the axis line and the enable path, and the launch falls back to this skill's own launch playbook without retrying run.
expectations: Opens the result block with 'invocation refused (disableBundledSkills)'
Names the axis line (settings or environment)
Names the enable path (disableBundledSkills, skillOverrides)
Falls back to this skill's own launch playbook, the project's documented start command
Does not retry the run invocation

evals.name: native-step-run-resolves-no-orchestrator
evals.prompt: /testing:run-e2e the login flow. The bundled run skill resolves in this session and the project has no orchestrator configuration.
evals.expected_output: No orchestrator governs the start and run resolves, so the drive subagent invokes run through the Skill tool to launch the app only. It fingerprints the tracked tree before and after the invocation, layers screenshots, responses, and logs on top of run's result, and records State: ran in the result block.
expectations: Invokes run through the Skill tool to launch the app and report how to reach it
Saves git diff HEAD to a scratch file immediately before and after the invocation and compares the two
Layers evidence (screenshots, responses, logs) on top of run's result
Records 'State: ran' in the result block
Launches the app once, through run only

evals.name: native-step-skipped-orchestrator-governs
evals.prompt: /testing:run-e2e the login flow. The project's docker-compose configuration governs the start, and the bundled run skill resolves in this session.
evals.expected_output: The project's orchestrator governs the start, so the Native step is skipped and the orchestrator path runs unchanged. The result block records the skip and run is never invoked, leaving one launch path.
expectations: Records 'skipped (orchestrator governs the start)' in the result block
Does not invoke run
Launches through the orchestrator path only, one launch path

evals.name: native-step-skipped-app-already-running

evals.expected_output: No orchestrator governs the start and run resolves, but the drive subagent probes the named URL before invoking run and gets a response. The Native step is skipped, run is never invoked, and the result block records the skip so no second instance starts.
expectations: Probes the named localhost URL or port before invoking run, passing it as one quoted argument
Records 'skipped (app already running)' in the result block
Does not invoke run
Drives the existing instance and launches nothing

evals.name: flow-suite-is-the-oracle
evals.prompt: /testing:run-e2e the checkout flow. The project has a committed @playwright/test suite under e2e/ with a checkout.spec.ts, and its README documents `npm run test:e2e`. The app is running.
evals.expected_output: Runs the committed checkout spec through the project's documented command before any ad-hoc driving, with traces kept for failed tests, and reports its pass or fail as the verdict for the checkout scenario. Ad-hoc driving and screenshots still run for the changed screens, but are reported as evidence, not as the verdict. A screenshot that looks right does not override a failing spec.
expectations: Runs the committed spec through the project's documented command before driving the app ad hoc
Reports the spec's pass or fail as the scenario verdict
Labels screenshots and the ad-hoc drive as evidence, not the oracle
Starts a trace before the ad-hoc drive and lists the trace path as an artifact

evals.name: failure-packet-handed-to-diagnose
evals.prompt: /testing:run-e2e the login flow. The committed login.spec.ts fails: the expect on the welcome heading times out. Playwright is 1.63.
evals.expected_output: Writes one failure packet for the failed scenario, with scenario, expected outcome taken from the requirement (not from what the app shows), actual, failing step as spec file and line, trace path, the `npx playwright trace action <n>` output for the failing expect, the error-context aria snapshot, new console errors, failed requests and screenshot path, each filled or saying why it is empty. The Handoff invokes /testing:diagnose with the packet as its input rather than a summary.
expectations: Writes a failure packet with every field filled or explained
States the expected outcome from the requirement, not from the app's current behavior
Includes the trace path and the trace action output for the failing action
Includes the error-context aria snapshot
Passes the packet to /testing:diagnose

evals.name: worst-case-network-injection
evals.prompt: /testing:run-e2e worst-case the member list on the team settings page
evals.expected_output: Parses worst-case as the action and the rest as the target. Reads context/worst-case.md and, when present, .claude/testing/worst-case.md as data. Maps every rendered field with source and limit, injects plausible worst-case values at the data boundary (mocking the HTTP response through /playwright:playwright when the list arrives over the network, so no file is written), renders at the real container width, 320px, the widest layout, approximated 200% zoom (named as an approximation), dark mode and right-to-left where supported, and reports What broke (severity, field, value, environment, fix with file:line, seen or inferred), Decisions for you, and What held up. Edits no component code.
expectations: The worst-case token is treated as the action, not as part of the scenario
Data is injected at the data boundary, preferring network mocking, never by editing markup or styles
The report has the three parts: what broke, decisions, what held up
The zoom check is named as an approximation

evals.name: worst-case-file-revert-proven
evals.prompt: /testing:run-e2e worst-case src/components/MemberList (its data comes from src/fixtures/members.json)
evals.expected_output: With file-bound data, checks src/fixtures/members.json is clean, saves git diff HEAD and git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all --ignored to scratch files outside the tree, backs up the fixture byte for byte, injects, renders, restores from the copy, re-snapshots and compares each pair with cmp, and reports the revert proof.
expectations: Both snapshots include untracked and ignored files (--untracked-files=all --ignored)
The fixture is restored from a byte-for-byte copy, not rewritten from memory
The report states the cmp result of the revert proof

evals.name: worst-case-dirty-target-refused

evals.expected_output: The target fixture is already dirty, so the action refuses to write it, says so, and stops (or uses network mocking if the data also arrives over HTTP) rather than overwriting the uncommitted edits.
expectations: The dirty fixture file is not written or overwritten
The answer says the file is dirty and why it refused

evals.name: worst-case-keep

expectations: The fixture is kept as a new file beside the demo data and its path is named
Changes other than the kept fixture are reverted
